what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A website where investors use our tools
sections.para: An article brief for investor.sgit.ai: because what we build has to be experienced, investors and founders should use it, with news, contracts as graphs, deal rooms as vaults, an evaluation framework and sgit as the case study, run by agents and shown to investors.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Eight lines from the brief to asking investors
sections.para: An article brief; experience explains; one site for investors and founders; eight sections; the lost evaluation framework returns; run by agents; built to the house rules with CI owning the version; then ask investors what helps.

sections.label: Why a website, and why for investors
sections.line: Investors should use the technology, not read about it
sections.para: Vaults, read keys, agents with keys and behaviour policies sound abstract until opened. The pieces exist on this site, the investor deck, the deal room vaults, the insurance calculator; what is missing is one place for investors and founders where they are the website.

sections.label: What it would hold
sections.line: News, contracts, founders, models, vaults, keys, cases
sections.para: Angel and Series A news as a graph; term sheets and cap tables linked clause to clause; a founders' section; funding models from open source to proprietary; deal rooms as vaults; keys for investors; sgit as a published case study and RiskMandate at work.

sections.label: Work that got lost: the evaluation framework
sections.line: The March framework scores security startups to forty
sections.para: The GenAI cybersecurity startup evaluation framework scores seven criteria and an architecture meta-criterion from 1 to 5, with bands from Rare to Avoid. It is not yet a maturity model: no levels, and no team, traction or financials, by design.

sections.label: Run by agents, fed by the newsroom
sections.line: A small scheduled agent team, fed by the newsroom's wire
sections.para: Like the PHP newsroom's two people and nineteen agents, but smaller: conductor, journalist, researcher, security and observability. The news could come from a newsroom wire vault the site reads, which shows what vaults are for.

sections.label: Built to the house rules from the first commit
sections.line: sgit.ai's repository rules, with CI owning the version
sections.para: A brief in full, a reality file, a corrections file, a gate, real tests, a review folder, roles as files, md twins and llms.txt, read keys only. CI picks every version; the site points to coding, nfrs and ux.sgit.ai.

sections.label: Then ask investors
sections.line: Show it to investors, and record what they say
sections.para: Once a first version runs, email investors and ask whether it is useful and what would help; the answers decide the site and go on the record.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: A brief: nothing built, and a framework not a model
sections.para: None of it is built; the framework scores but has no levels; the news needs public sources and no private names; The Cyber Boardroom repository's link is to come; sgit's raise is not published.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Two memos, a research agent, and a build brief
sections.para: From Dinis's two memos of 28 October, kept word for word; the framework, the PHP newsroom and sgit.ai's guidance read from their own pages on 29 October; the build brief for the site's agent is in the repository notes.
